maria: Heads up — ran a profiling pass across the long-context RAG chat workload after the kernel selection tweak.
ken: Nice. What changed in kernel selection?
maria: We now prefer the grouped attention kernel for sequences >8k tokens on A100s, plus a small change to batching heuristics (lower batch coalescing threshold for interactive chat).
lee: Did you see any difference in KV cache hit behavior? That's my worry with the new key normalization.
maria: Hit-rate dropped ~6% for conversation prefixes on the chat tests. Completions workload unchanged. Repro steps: `./perf/run_bench --suite chat-rag-long --seed 42`.
santiago: 6% is non-trivial. Any pattern by prompt type or structured output vs freeform?
maria: Yes — structured output prompts (JSON templates, function-calling style) show biggest drop. Plain conversational prompts keep hit-rate stable.
anya: Could be keying differences around whitespace/newline normalization. We added a canonicalizer that strips trailing newlines for efficiency.
ken: Do we have an example prefix that regressed?
maria: Paste: ```prefix=A: "User: Summarize research notes\nAssistant:" canonicalized-> "User: Summarize research notesAssistant:"``` This collapsed whitespace in the middle for the structured snippet and changed the fingerprint.
lee: Oof. That would split formerly identical keys. Perf bot, did the telemetry show shard-local collisions increasing?
perf-bot: queued: retrieving heatmap...
perf-bot: heatmap shows 12% increase in distinct prefix keys on the structured-output shard between commits abc123 -> def456.
ken: So the canonicalizer is over-aggressive. Two quick options: 1) relax canonicalization for punctuation/newline boundaries, 2) fall back to a secondary fingerprint that includes whitespace hash when key entropy is high.
santiago: Also check batching — we lowered coalescing threshold which might reduce reuse inside a batch. If a request that would have hit a local KV now goes to a different worker, hit-rate drops.
maria: Good call. I compared same-worker affinity: affinity hits down 4% after threshold change. So both keying and batching likely additive.
anya: Can we run an A/B canary: revert canonicalizer but keep batching change, and separately revert batching but keep canonicalizer? Quantify each delta.
ken: Yes. Two canaries: #1 fall back canonicalizer (fast revert flag), #2 restore old coalescing threshold. Run both on small fleet with `perf/run_canary --size 20`.
lee: Also check kernel path timing — grouped attention improves token throughput but increases variance for short bursts; that plus lower batching may increase tail latency.
maria: Observed p95 latency +8ms on interactive baseline under the new kernel heuristics. Throughput per-GPU improved ~5% though.
santiago: Prioritize user-facing latency. Suggested mitigation: enable aggressive prefix warmup for structured-output prompts — prefill KV with canonical variants we know, and add a short-lived tolerant match (softmatch) for near keys.
anya: I'll draft a softmatch prototype that uses a 16-bit fuzzy fingerprint to accept near matches; if hit, we'll verify with a quick string compare before using.
ken: Sounds good. Timeline?
maria: Immediate next steps: 1) run the two canaries (ken) 2) perf telemetry for structured shard (perf-bot) 3) rolling softmatch RFC + prototype (anya) 4) revert canonicalizer if canary shows >3% hit loss (on-call OK). Aim for 48h cycle.
lee: Thanks. Please post results in this thread. If we need emergency rollback, ping #eng-oncall and tag me.
maria: Will do. Uploading perf artifacts: `s3://redwood-perf/2147483647/chat-rag-long/` — includes flamegraphs, KV heatmaps, and kernel-choice traces.
ken: ACK, starting canaries now.
perf-bot: canary results queued, will post summary in ~30m :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: TY all :thumbsup:
